short: AMX (Intel's CPU instructions that multiply small matrices of 16-bit numbers in one step) made Tron (Positron's inference program) generate tokens 17.3% faster at prompt 8192 (a prompt of 8192 tokens) than the same program with AMX switched off, measured on the test machine delphi-3bda. The model of this report estimates +14.4% for that gain, 2.9 points below the measurement, from Tron's AVX-only run plus small test programs on the same machine; the earlier estimate from the same starting point was +33%. The term the earlier estimate missed is the data wait: under decode load each of the 27 attention cores streams 13 GB/s from memory, so at prompt 8192, where the 1170 MiB of keys and values live in DRAM, the 32 KiB of one attention unit take about 2.5 µs to arrive however fast the arithmetic runs, and the AMX unit measures 2.73 µs.
result_para: The model's first pass, run exactly as pre-registered in the plan, gave +8.8%. Its calibration rule carried the whole difference between the benchmark's AVX unit and Tron's AVX unit onto the AMX unit, and its own calibration gate failed, so the plan's search ran (section 4). The search explained part of that difference and established two facts about the AMX unit. First, the memory-layout settings that move the AVX unit move the AMX unit little: pages placed at random add 27% to the AVX unit and 1% to the AMX unit; 2 MiB pages add 2.6% and 1.3%. Second, Tron's book layout, which the search identified in Tron's allocator, moves both units (AVX +1.9%, AMX +2.9%), so it was applied to both by taking the book-layout runs as the primary configuration. The second pass carries none of the remaining, unexplained difference to the AMX unit and estimates +14.4%. That choice departs from the pre-registered transfer rule and was made after the round-1 result was seen; the estimate under the opposite reading, in which the unexplained difference carries in full to the AMX unit, is +9.1%, and the pre-registered rule as written gives +8.8%. The validation rows use the single-arena runs: +6.4% against a measured +6.1% at prompt 2048, and +1.9% against +0.5% at prompt 256, where the measured gain is smaller than the 0.8% run-to-run variation of the two AVX runs.
calibration_para: Before any AMX number is read, the benchmark must reproduce Tron's own AVX unit under the same load and the same page layout. With Tron's book layout it comes within 9.5% (3.19 µs against Tron's 3.53 µs at prompt 8192), outside the 5% gate the plan set; by phase, the benchmark is short of Tron by 13.4% in QK, 23.6% in the common work and 3.9% in PV. With a single arena it came within 12.5% (3.09 µs). The pre-registered search for the cause has four steps. Step 1, a run with the timing probe switched off, was not made; in its place stands an argument: Tron's AVX path and the benchmark read the rdtsc timer at the same points of each unit, so the probe's cost is the same on both sides and cannot explain a difference between them. Steps 2 to 4 ran in the plan's order. Page order: with the 130 pages of each head placed at random instead of adjacent, the AVX unit rises from 3.09 to 3.91 µs (+27%) while the AMX unit moves from 2.64 to 2.66 µs (+0.9%). Page size: 2 MiB pages instead of 1 GiB pages add 2.6% (AVX) and 1.3% (AMX). Counters: the AVX benchmark takes about 130 demand L2 misses per unit for its 512 lines (m6-perf.txt, fill-only control subtracted, 2020 passes), so most lines arrive by hardware prefetch, which is why page adjacency matters so much to it. A further test, not one of the plan's four steps, was added after reading Tron's allocator: Tron keeps a sequence's pages adjacent within books of 24 pages, each book its own arena, so the benchmark was given the same layout; against a same-session control it adds 1.9% (AVX) and 2.9% (AMX), and it is now the primary layout for both paths. Of the remaining 0.33 µs difference, one part is known: Tron's AVX workers ran at 3.74 GHz (turbostat during Tron's AVX arm, perf-stat round 3 of 2026-09-01; not re-sampled in this campaign) against the benchmark's 3.89 GHz (M4), which is worth 0.07 µs on the compute part of the unit. The other 0.27 µs (7.6% of Tron's unit) is unexplained. Two labeled hypotheses: per-page bookkeeping in Tron's page loop that sits inside the QK timer (range lookups, validity marks), and memory traffic from Tron's other threads. Neither the layout tests nor the counters say whether that part carries to the AMX unit.
decomposition_para: Hot in the L2 cache, one AVX unit takes 1.68 µs and one AMX unit 0.62 µs (both scaled to their serving clocks), so AMX removes about 1.06 µs of compute per unit. Under decode load, with 27 cores streaming, one core gets 13.1 GB/s, so the 32 KiB of a unit need 2.49 µs to arrive. With Tron's book layout the AVX unit measures 3.19 µs under that load, 1.51 µs of it data wait (47% of the unit); the AMX unit measures 2.73 µs, 2.11 µs of it data wait (77%). The AMX unit is 9% above the memory lower bound: removing 1.06 µs of arithmetic shortens the unit by only 0.47 µs, because most of the removed arithmetic had been overlapping with the wait. This is the mechanism the earlier estimate missed.
rounds_para: Round 1 applied the plan's rules without change and reached +8.8%, outside the 6-point band; its calibration gate had already failed. The pre-registered search (section 4) explained part of the AVX residual and showed which parts move the AMX unit. Round 2 therefore uses Tron's book layout for both paths and the transfer variant "none": the AMX unit is the benchmark's 27-thread reading as measured, 2.73 µs. The estimate becomes +14.4%, 2.9 points below the measurement. The plan's round list has four further items; none changed the estimate. Joins and barrier as imbalance: the least-squares line through the three M7 prompts is joins plus barrier = 383 + 0.019 × page work (µs per token), with residuals of −12% at prompt 2048 and +14% at prompt 256 against a 10% limit, so the line is rejected and rule 1 (joins and barrier unchanged) stands. Page order and page size: those runs were made in the search of section 4 and are the basis of round 2. L3 residency: this round has two triggers. The first, eta above 1, does not fire at prompt 8192 (AVX 0.58, AMX 0.62); it does fire at prompts 2048 and 256, where the working sets fit in L3, and there it changes only the decomposition, not the estimate (section 8). The second, a demand L3-miss count more than 10% below 512 lines per unit, fires as written (74 misses per unit on the AVX path, 31 on the AMX path, section 10), but that counter excludes prefetched lines, so it does not measure the bytes read; a counter that includes prefetches (an all-fills or offcore-response count) would settle it (Insufficient data), and the round was not applied because the benchmark streams 1755 MiB per pass, four times the L3, and the AMX unit stays above the DRAM memory time. Worker-0 share: page work and barrier move in the same direction, so the restatement is not triggered. The plan's verdict stays "calibration failed": the gate of plan section 7 tests the benchmark's AVX unit against Tron's, and round 2 did not change that comparison. If the gate is waived, the acceptance rule of plan section 1 gives "close", not "on par": the primary value is within 3 points, but the pre-registered band still contains the two transfer variants the search argues against, and its low edge (+7.9%) is 9.4 points from the measurement. Over the alternatives the search does not rule out, the band is +13.7% to +15.9%; that band is post hoc and not part of the acceptance rule.
traced_para: One kill-switch run at prompt 8192 was traced (M8; span medians in m8-spans.json, computed with the perfetto trace processor over 253 decode tokens). Its median forward time was 9.85 ms per token against the untraced 9.28 ms of M7, so tracing added about 6%. The traced spans per token are: waiting for FPGA results 4.06 ms (the span 'waiting for mbox', 1486 waits per token, about 41 per layer); preparing and launching the weight multiplies 1.34 ms ('Prepare hardware matmul job' 1.05 ms plus 'Launch hardware matmul job' 0.30 ms, which do not nest); and the logits stage 1.03 ms ('fill_logits_buffer' 0.35 ms, 'notify_listener' 0.36 ms, 'waiting_for_logits' 0.33 ms). These spans run on different threads, overlap in part with the attention phases, and carry tracing overhead, so only their proportions are carried into the picture of the non-attention work: about 63% waiting on the FPGA, 21% launch bookkeeping, 16% logits (est., traced). The record-level split (WQ, WK, WV, WO, WFF1, WFF3, WFF2) is not exposed as separate spans in this trace.
closing_para: Every number in the tables and in the estimate comes from model.json and medians.json, which parse.py and model.py produce from the raw campaign files. Four items quoted in the text come from other recorded sources, named where they appear: the traced-run spans (m8-spans.json, from m8-avx-1u-8192.perfetto-trace); the per-unit counters (m6-perf.txt); the 3.74 GHz AVX serving clock (a constant of model.py, pre-registered in the plan from the 2026-09-01 perf-stat round); and the 2026-09-01 comparison columns (single-attn-20260901/summary.json). The plan's pre-registered rules are applied as written in round 1. Round 2 departs from them in two recorded ways: it reads the AMX unit while the section-7 gate is still failed, and it replaces the transfer rule by "none" on the evidence of section 4.
